title: Notes on the electron and hole density in solid state physics
summary: A field-theory perspective on electron and hole occupations: quantising the Schrödinger field in a Bloch basis and recovering the Fermi–Dirac distribution.

footnotes: In solid state physics, the energy spectrum of the Hamiltonian generally has several bands, which may be separated by gaps.

From the point of view of the scalar Schrödinger equation alone, the introduction of the $s$ label is additional input. However, the electron’s Schrödinger equation is a low-energy approximation of the Dirac equation, which is a theory for spinors. In the noninteracting approximation used here, spin-dependent terms vanish when magnetic fields and relativistic corrections are neglected. The one-particle Hamiltonian is then $h = (\mathbf{p}^2/(2m)+V(\mathbf{x}))\otimes I_2$.
